section_summary: The section concludes a technical list of changes to Japanese radio call signs and emergency police radio registrations, including frequencies, emissions, station locations, and corrections to an earlier July list. It then documents a diplomatic exchange concerning interference on Japan's 4495-kilocycle aircraft-control frequency from a station in North Korea. The Soviet Foreign Ministry declined to assist because the alleged source lay outside Soviet territory.

subfiles.title: Changes of Call Sign and Emergency Police Radio Lists (continuation)
subfiles.about: Lists changes and corrections to Japanese radio call signs and emergency police radio registrations.
subfiles.summary: Radio list continuation: changed call signs or frequencies at Osaka, Hikone and Tokyo and for portable stations in coastal waters, then emergency police stations nationwide with registration numbers, frequencies, call signs, restrictions, addresses and coordinates; heavy type marks changes.

subfiles.title: Incoming Telegram No. 3176 Concerning the Soviet Reply on Radio Interference
subfiles.about: Reports the substance of the Soviet Foreign Ministry's reply concerning interference with a radio frequency used in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Telegram 3176: a Soviet note of December 15 says the interfering station is outside the Soviet Union and gives no sign of help ending the interference; full text to follow.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 809: Radio Interference Experienced by Aircraft Control Tower Frequency in Japan
subfiles.about: Forwards and explains the Soviet response to a protest about North Korean interference on Japan's aircraft-control frequency.
subfiles.summary: Despatch 809: after the Department's October 4 telegram on a North Korean station interfering with the 4495-kilocycle aircraft-control frequency, registered by the U.S. since October 27, 1938, Embassy note 577 sought Soviet help; Soviet note 83 replied only that the station wasn't in Soviet territory.

subfiles.title: Translation of Soviet Ministry of Foreign Affairs Note No. 83
subfiles.from: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the USSR
subfiles.to: Embassy of the United States of America, Moscow
subfiles.about: Declines the American request for Soviet assistance in ending radio interference allegedly originating at Hamhung in North Korea.
subfiles.summary: Translation of Soviet Note 83: it can't stop alleged interference on 4495 kilocycles from a Hamhung, North Korea station, since the station is outside Soviet territory.
